learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the invisible backbone of business! Learn how banking, insurance, communication, and warehousing make trade possible.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Services are intangible (you can't touch them), inconsistent (every experience is slightly different), inseparable (production and consumption happen at the same time), and cannot be stored (no inventory).
Banks accept deposits and lend money. Modern business relies on E-Banking (NEFT, RTGS, IMPS, ATMs) to transfer funds instantly, anywhere, anytime, reducing the need for physical cash.

Insurance protects business from risks. Key principles include 'Utmost Good Faith' (hiding nothing), 'Insurable Interest' (you must suffer a loss if the thing is damaged), and 'Indemnity' (insurance is for compensation, not to make a profit).
Goods aren't always sold immediately after production. Warehouses store goods safely, bridge the time gap between production and consumption, and stabilize prices.

fun_activity.title: 🔥 The Profit Test
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine you bought a ₹50,000 phone and insured it for ₹60,000. It gets stolen. Will the insurance company pay you ₹60,000? No! The Principle of Indemnity says you will only get the actual value (₹50,000). You cannot make a profit out of a loss!

exam_tips: 📌 The 5 I's of services: Intangibility, Inconsistency, Inseparability, Inventory (less), and Involvement.
📌 RTGS (Real Time Gross Settlement) is for large transactions (minimum ₹2 Lakhs), while NEFT processes transactions in batches.
📌 Be ready to explain the Principle of 'Subrogation' and 'Contribution' in insurance with simple examples.
quick_recap: ⭐ Life insurance has an element of both protection and investment, whereas fire/marine insurance is pure protection.
⭐ Telecom services and postal services form the communication backbone of business.
⭐ Bonded warehouses are used to store imported goods until custom duties are paid.
